newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle sales brisk at $63,dn $1-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle sales brisk at $63,dn $1-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $63.00 per cwt in active trading late Tuesday, down $1.00 from light sales on Monday and last week's moderate volume, feedlot sources said.
About 25,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area and near 25,000 in Kansas, sources said.

Lower beef prices quoted by USDA at midday dashed some cattle feeders' optimism for firmer cattle prices, sources said. Beef prices were pressured by large slaughter last week and outlooks for waning demand now that retailer buying for Independence Day advertisements has ended.
Beef prices Tuesday were quoted down $0.34 to $1.40 per cwt, with 305 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. Choice beef weighing 700-850 lbs was quoted at $103.61, down $0.36 from Monday.

Scattered sales of beef for the holiday next week could still occur but Friday is the latest day beef could be shipped in order to arrive at retailers in time, said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean Witter Reynolds.
Fed cattle prices also were pressured by outlooks for increased contracted cattle supplies that will become available to packers after July 1, Benson said.
